Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:11:1.hebrew: בעטה מהלכת ברבוצה פטורה - ואף על גב דברה"ר חייבת, הכא פטורה, דכל המשנה — כגון זו שרבצה ברה"ר — ובא אחר כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:11:1.english: [If the] walking [cow] kicked the prone [cow], [its owner is] exempt - Even though in the public domain [an owner] is [ordinarily] liable, here [the owner] is exempt, for anyone who deviates [from the norm] — such as this [cow] that lay down in the public domain — and another comes [and deviates with respect to it, is exempt], etc.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:13:1.english: They rest - They stop to rest.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:13:2.english: [For] an animal, it is not its way - To lie down.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:14:1.hebrew: דמי עמיר - שאם אכלה שעורין כדי שביעתה, אינו משלם לו אלא דמים שהיה צריך ליתן בקשין ובתבן להאכילה, דאמר ליה: אי אפשי להאכילה שעורין, אלא קשין ותבן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:14:1.english: The value of stalks - For if [the animal] ate barley to its fill, he pays him only the money that he would have needed to spend on stubble and straw to feed it, for he says to him: "I do not wish to feed it barley, only stubble and straw."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:14:2.hebrew: דמי שעורין בזול - כפי שהיה צריך ליקח שעורין למאכלה, אם היה רוצה להאכילה שעורין, ולא יתן לו כשער שבשוק, דלמא איהו לא מאכיל לה שעורין; אלא בזול יתן, כדאמרינן בפרק מי שמת (ב"ב קמו:), וכל זוזא חשיב בארבע דנקי, דהיינו שני שלישי הדמים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:14:2.english: The value of barley cheaply - According to what he would have needed to buy barley for its food, had he wanted to feed it barley, and he does not give him according to the market rate, [since] perhaps he would not feed it barley. Rather, he gives [at] a cheap [rate], as we say in chapter Mi Shemet (Bava Batra 146b), and every zuz is reckoned at four danki, which is two-thirds of the value.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:16:1.hebrew: אע"פ שאינו רגיל - להאכילה שעורין אלא עמיר, משלם לו דמי שעורין כפי מה שאדם אחר רגיל ליתן לבהמתו קב או קביים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:16:1.english: Even though he is not accustomed - to feed it barley, rather [he feeds it] straw, he pays him the value of barley according to what another person is accustomed to give his animal, a kav or two kavim.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:16:2.english: Therefore - since we assess [the benefit] according to something fit for it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:16:3.hebrew: אכלה חטים או כל דבר הרע לה - דלא נהנית, פטורה ברשות הרבים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:16:3.english: If it ate wheat or anything that is bad for it - Since it did not derive benefit, [it] is exempt in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:17:1.hebrew: בתחומא - לא היית קרוב אצלנו שתוכל לבא. ל"א: בתחומא — בבית המדרש. ראשון שמעתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:17:1.english: Within [our] boundary - You were not near us so that you could come. Another explanation: "within [our] boundary" [means] in the study hall. I heard the first [explanation].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: אי נימא בחצר דלא קיימא לאגרא וגברא דלא עביד למיגר, זה לא נהנה וזה לא חסר. דלא עביד למיגר — זה שדר באותה חצר אינו עשוי לשכור חצרות, לפי שמצויין לו בתים להשאיל או יש לו בית אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:1.english: This is the reading: "If we say [that the case concerns] a courtyard that does not stand to be rented out, and a man who is not accustomed to rent, this one does not derive benefit and that one does not suffer a loss." "Who is not accustomed to rent" — [meaning] this [person] who lives in that courtyard is not accustomed to rent courtyards, because houses are readily available to him to borrow, or he has another house.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:2.english: This [one] does not derive benefit - For houses are readily available to him for free.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:3.hebrew: וזה לא חסר - דהא לא קיימא לאגרא, ופשיטא דפטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:3.english: And that [one] does not suffer a loss - Since it does not stand to be rented out, and it is obvious that he is exempt [from paying].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:4.english: This [one] derives benefit - For behold, he would have had to rent another house.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:5.hebrew: וזה חסר - דחצרו קיימא להשכיר, והוה מוגר לאחריני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:18:5.english: And that [one] suffers a loss - For his courtyard stands to be rented out, and he would have rented [it] to others.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:19:1.english: That does not stand to be rented out, and a man who would rent - For it is [a case of] "this one benefits and that one does not lose."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:19:2.english: What loss have I caused you - Behold, even without this, you do not rent [it] out.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:3:1.hebrew: בקופצת - שקפצה ואכלה על צוארה, שאין דרכה בכך, ותולדה דקרן הוא, וחייבת חצי נזק קאמר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:3:1.english: With regard to a jumping [animal] - That it jumped and ate over its neck, for that is not its normal manner, and it is a derivative of Goring, and [the baraita] means [that] it is liable for half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:5:1.hebrew: כגון דקיימא עמיר ברשות הניזק - ובהמה ברשות הרבים, ומגלגלת ואתי מרשות היחיד לרשות הרבים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:5:1.english: For example, where a sheaf is standing in the injured party's domain - And the animal [is] in the public domain, and it rolls [it], and [the sheaf] comes from the private domain to the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:5:2.hebrew: מאי - בתר אכילה אזלינן ופטורה, או בתר דשקלה ליה אזלינן וחייבת? והוא הדין נמי אי בהמה ברשות הניזק ועמיר ברשות הרבים וגילגלתו מרשות הרבים לרשות היחיד — אי בתר אכילה אזלינן, חייבת, ואי בתר דשקלה ליה אזלינן, פטורה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:5:2.english: What [is the halakha] - Do we follow [the place of] the eating, and [the animal] is exempt, or do we follow [the place] from where it took it, and it is liable? And the same law applies as well if an animal is in the domain of the injured party and a sheaf is in the public domain, and [the animal] rolled it from the public domain to the private domain — if we follow [the place of] the eating, it is liable, and if we follow [the place] from where it took it, it is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:6:1.hebrew: משוי - קס"ד אמתחת מלאה שעורין, ואכלה בפנים, חייבת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:6:1.english: A load - It was initially assumed [that this refers to] a sack full of barley, and [if an animal] ate inside [the private property], [its owner] is liable.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:6:2.hebrew: מאי לאו - כגון שאכלתו כולו, והכי קאמר: אכלתו בפנים — כגון שגלגלה את כולו בפנים — חייבת; גילגלתו לחוץ — פטורה. אלמא בתר אכילה אזלינן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:6:2.english: What, is it not - [That the case is] such where [the animal] ate all of it, and this is what [the baraita] is saying: [If] it ate it inside — for instance, where it rolled all of it inside — [the owner is] liable; [if] it rolled it outside — [the owner is] exempt. Evidently, we follow [the place of] eating.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:6:3.hebrew: אימא אכלה על מה שבחוץ פטורה - על מה שהיה מונח מתחילה בחוץ פטורה, ועל המונח בתחילה בפנים חייבת, דבתר דשקלה ליה אזלינן, בין היא בפנים בין היא בחוץ:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:6:3.english: Say: It ate; for that which is outside, [it is] exempt - For that which was initially lying outside, [the owner is] exempt; and for that which was initially lying inside, [the owner is] liable, for we follow [the place from] where [the animal] took it, whether it is inside or whether it is outside.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:7:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא - לעולם כדקתני: אכלתו בפנים חייבת על כולו, אכלתו בחוץ פטורה על כולו, ולא תפשוט דגלגול מלתא הוא. דכי א"ר חייא — בפתילה דאספסתא, משוי של שחת שעליו ארוכין, וראשו אחד בפנים וראשו אחד בחוץ, דכיון דהאי רישא כי גריר ליה אזיל אידך בתריה, כמאן דמנח כולו בחד דוכתא דמי, הלכך אזלינן בתר בהמה. כי קמיבעיא לן — כגון שעורין, דכוליה גרעין קאי בפנים או בחוץ, וכי אכלה האי, לא אזיל האי בתריה אי לא מגלגלה ליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:7:1.english: And if you wish, say - Actually, [it is] as it was taught: [if] it ate it inside, [the owner] is liable for all of it; [if] it ate it outside, [the owner] is exempt for all of it, and do not resolve [from this] that rolling is a [determinative] factor. For when Rabbi Chiyya stated [his ruling, it was] regarding a stalk of fodder — a bundle of green fodder whose leaves are long, with one end of it inside and one end of it outside; for since when [the animal] drags this end, the other [end] goes after it, it is considered as though all of it were resting in one place; therefore, we follow [the location of] the animal. When we have a dilemma, [it is in a case] such as barley, where each entire kernel stands inside or outside, and when [the animal] eats this one, that one does not go after it unless it rolls it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:7:2.hebrew: פתילה - על שם דארוך הוא, קרי ליה פתילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:7:2.english: A wick [petilah] - Because it is long, [the Gemara] calls it a wick [petilah].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:9:1.hebrew: אכולהו - הא דקתני מתניתין ברה"ר פטורה, אכולהו קאי, ואפילו אכסות וכלים, דשינוי הוה ותולדה דקרן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:9:1.english: To all of [them] - That which the Mishnah teaches, [that] in the public domain it is exempt, refers to all of them, and even to garments and vessels, which is an unusual [act] and a derivative of Horn.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:9:2.hebrew: כל המשנה - כגון זה שהניח כסותו וכליו ברה"ר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:9:2.english: Anyone who deviates - For example, this [person] who placed his garment and his vessels in the public domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 20a:9:3.english: And another came and deviated with regard to him - For example, this [animal] that ate it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:11:1.hebrew: ואזדא ריש לקיש לטעמיה - תרוייהו צריכי: הך דהכא צריכא, דלא נימא: כסות — עבדי אינשי דמנחי גלימא ומתפחי; וההיא דב' פרות אשמועינן: דוקא בעטה רבוצה במהלכת — חייבת, הא הוזקה — פטורה, כדדייק לקמן פרק המניח (בבא קמא דף לב.), דאבעי לה לסגויי באידך גיסא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:11:1.english: And Reish Lakish follows his [own] reasoning - Both [statements] are necessary: This [ruling] here is necessary so that we would not say [that regarding] garments, people normally put down a cloak [in the public domain] and rest, [so it is not a deviation]; and that [ruling] of the two cows teaches us [that] specifically [when] the prone [cow] kicked the walking [cow] is [its owner] liable, whereas if [the walking cow] was injured [by the prone cow, the owner of the prone cow] is exempt, as [the Gemara] infers later in chapter HaMeniach (Bava Kamma 32a), because [the walking cow] should have walked on the other side.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:18:1.hebrew: זה אין נהנה וזה אין חסר הוא - אפילו בחצר דקיימא לאגרא וגברא דלא עביד למיגר, הו"מ למימר דפטור, כיון שלא נהנה, אע"פ שגרם הפסד לחבירו; דאפילו גירשו חבירו מביתו ונעל דלת בפניו, אין זה אלא גרמא בעלמא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:18:1.english: "It is [a case of] this [one] does not derive benefit, and that [one] does not suffer a loss" - Even in [the case of] a courtyard that stands to be rented out and a person who does not normally rent, [the Gemara] could have said that he is exempt since he did not derive benefit, even though he caused a loss to his fellow; for even if his fellow evicted him from his house and locked the door before him, this is nothing more than mere indirect causation [gerama].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:18:2.hebrew: זה נהנה וזה חסר הוא - דכל זמן שרואין את זה עומד בביתו, אין מבקשין ממנו להשכיר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:18:2.english: This one derives benefit and that one suffers a loss - For as long as [people] see this [person] residing in his house, they do not ask him to rent [it out].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:5:1.hebrew: מתגלגל מהו - פ"ה, דמספקא ליה אי בתר אכילה אזלינן ואי בתר לקיחה. וקשה, דלקמן (בבא קמא דף כא:) גבי כלב שנטל חררה והלך לגדיש, פשיטא לן דאי אכליה בגדיש דעלמא דפטור; ועוד, דלשון "מתגלגל" לא משמע הכי. ונראה לר"י: כגון דקיימי פירות ברשות הניזק ומגלגלי ואתו לרשות הרבים, דאי לאו שהבהמה מעכבתן בפיה ואכלתן שם היה סופן להניח ברשות הרבים, וקמבעיא ליה אי חשיבי כמונחים ברשות הרבים או לאו. וקאמר: ת"ש, "משוי מקצתו בפנים כו'", מאי לאו במתגלגל — דאורחיה דמילתא כך היא במקצתו מבפנים ומקצתו מבחוץ — וקתני: "אכלה בפנים חייבת" — אע"פ שסופו להתגלגל בחוץ אם לא שאכלתן — ו"אכלה בחוץ פטורה" תנא אגב רישא, דמילתא דפשיטא היא. אימא: "על מה שבפנים חייבת" — פירוש: על מה שראוי להיות בפנים, שאין סופו להתגלגל בחוץ, חייבת. ואיבעית אימא: "בפתילה דאספסתא" — שעליו ארוכים, וסד"א ניזול בתר רוב עלה שבפנים או בחוץ:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 20a:5:1.english: "If [it was] rolling, what is [the halakha]?" - Rashi explained that he [Rabbi Zeira] is uncertain whether we follow [the place of] eating or we follow [the place of] taking. And [this is] difficult, for later (Bava Kamma 21b), regarding a dog that took a cake [of bread] and went to a stack of grain, it is obvious to us that if it ate it in someone else's stack of grain, [its owner] is exempt; and furthermore, the wording "rolling" does not imply this. Rather, it appears to Rabbeinu Yitzchak [that the case is] for example where produce is situated in the injured party's domain and is rolling along toward the public domain, such that were it not for the animal holding it back in its mouth and eating it there, it would have ended up resting in the public domain; and he raises the dilemma whether it is considered as resting in the public domain or not. And [the Gemara] says: Come and hear [a proof from the baraita]: "A load, partly inside, etc." — is this not referring to [produce] rolling, for such is the nature of a thing [that is] partly inside and partly outside? And it teaches: "[If] it ate inside, [its owner] is liable" — even though it would have ended up rolling outside had it not eaten it — while "[if] it ate outside, [its owner] is exempt" was taught incidentally because of the first clause, as it is an obvious matter. [The Gemara answers:] Say: "For that which is inside, [its owner] is liable" — meaning, for that which is fit to remain inside, which will not end up rolling outside, [its owner] is liable. And if you wish, say: "[It is referring to] a stalk of fodder [aspasta]" — whose leaves are long, and you might have thought to say that we should follow the majority of the leaf, whether [it is] inside or outside.
